conventions.convention: Weights are symmetric, nonnegative and zero-diagonal; support edges have strictly positive weight. Isolated vertices are singleton components. The energy is E(f)=½ fᵀLf, and anchoring requires every component meeting U to meet the nonempty boundary B.

Pseudo-label predictions within a round use the same training list. Distance ties use stable record indices, vote ties use the smallest class index, threshold equality is accepted, and appended pseudo-labels are never revised.
The randomized predictor distribution Q is identical under the two laws, which differ only at an unseen positive-mass atom. The risk is binary zero-one population risk.

The graph procedure uses exact real arithmetic and increasing vertex order. Its cap is per label coordinate and includes right-hand-side formation, a freshly recomputed Cholesky factor, substitutions and residual calculation. Validation, graph construction, component scans, loop control and budget checks are excluded.
The Cholesky recurrence uses indices 1 through n and returns a lower-triangular factor with positive diagonal, with M=RRᵀ.

load_bearing.statement: For a finite symmetric nonnegative zero-diagonal weighted graph with nonempty boundary B, assume every support component meeting U=V\B also meets B. The energy E(f)=½ fᵀLf with prescribed boundary values has exactly one minimizer. If U is empty it is the boundary vector; otherwise L_UU is real symmetric positive definite and f_U=−L_UU⁻¹L_UB y_B. Every unlabeled value is a positive-degree weighted neighbor average and lies between the minimum and maximum boundary values. For C≥2, coordinatewise extensions of one-hot boundary values have every row in the probability simplex.
For n≥1 and real symmetric positive-definite M, the displayed columnwise Cholesky recurrence has every pivot positive and returns a lower-triangular matrix R with positive diagonal satisfying M=RRᵀ.

On a finite discrete feature set, let two binary deterministic label laws have the same feature marginal μ and differ only at an unobserved atom x★ of mass q>0, outside a nonempty observed-input set. For any common probability vector Q on all binary predictors, the maximum of the two expected zero-one population risks is at least q/2.

For the specified finite weighted graph, nonempty boundary B and prescribed real boundary values, a graph-harmonic label extension is any minimizer of E(f)=½ fᵀLf over functions with those boundary values; the definition itself makes no uniqueness assertion.

The specified finite weighted k-nearest-record procedure adds all threshold-qualified pseudo-labels simultaneously in each round, never revises an added label, and returns its final classifier, log, remaining unlabeled set and stopping status. It makes no population-risk or pseudo-label-correctness guarantee.

published_dependencies.used_for: Real positive definiteness and the lower-triangular positive-diagonal factorization convention in the recurrence lemma and harmonic-extension theorem.
Invertibility of finite square matrices with zero kernel in the recurrence lemma's Schur-complement argument.
Existence and uniqueness of the real Cholesky factor of the anchored principal Laplacian block.
Correctness and uniqueness of the two triangular solves in the harmonic-extension theorem and graph propagation procedure.
Solving the positive-definite block system through its Cholesky factor in finitely many scalar operations.
The precise substitution recursions underlying the cited triangular-solve theorem.
